parts.content: Read the code around the predicate and canary, then write the KLEE harness.

I wrote the harness to `/tmp/locus-SND001/repo/__locus_harness_channels.c`. I haven't run it through KLEE, so there is no verdict yet.

**Data flow:** `paf_fmt.channels` is an `int`. It is read from the file header at lines 171–176. Nothing between the canary (line 206) and the predicate (line 212) changes it. Because of that, the harness can use a single symbolic `channels` variable. It doesn't need to model the surrounding code.

**How the harness works:**
- `channels` is symbolic.
- `klee_assume(!(channels >= 1 && channels <= SF_MAX_CHANNELS))` restricts KLEE to values the predicate would reject.
- `klee_assert(!((channels < 1) || (channels > SF_MAX_CHANNELS)))` is the canary condition, negated.

The assumption is the exact complement of the assertion. KLEE will therefore report a violation on any input, and the predicate will be flagged as unsound. This follows the pattern you gave, so I kept it.

I gave `SF_MAX_CHANNELS` a fallback value of 1024 in case the header isn't included. I didn't check that value against the repo's headers. Confirm it matches before relying on the result.
